# v0.3.50 — "Requires 2FA" means a person approves each run

**Upgrading from 0.3.49:**

- Rebuild and recreate the app container (`docker compose up -d --build alexclaw-prod`). No configuration or database change.
- A workflow that requires 2FA can no longer have a schedule: saving one with both is refused, whichever is set second ("cannot be set on a workflow that requires 2FA: each run needs a person's approval"). An existing workflow that already has both is left as it is but is no longer scheduled — it runs only from the admin UI's Run button or Telegram `/run`, each time with a code.
- A workflow that requires 2FA is refused, with a logged reason, on every route that cannot ask a person for a code: schedules, MCP, the cluster trigger (`send_to_workflow`), the GitHub webhook and skills calling `SkillAPI.run_workflow`. It is no longer listed as an MCP tool.
- The "Requires 2FA" checkbox is stored as a boolean, and every part of AlexClaw reads the flag the same way (a stored `"true"` or `"on"` counts as set). Before, the edit form showed a stored `"true"` as unchecked, so saving the form could drop the protection.

## Changes

- Each run of a workflow that requires 2FA carries a person's approval: after a second-factor code is verified — in the admin UI or on Telegram — that one run of that workflow is approved. An approval is single-use and short-lived (60 seconds), and cannot be reused for another run or another workflow.
- The workflow executor refuses a protected workflow without an approval, before any run is recorded.
- The scheduler never schedules a protected workflow.
